name: Question 10
problem:
| **Height ($x$)** | **$64$** | **$68$** | **$72$** | **$76$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Weight ($y$)** | $130$ | $148$ | $164$ | $186$ |

The table above shows the heights, in inches, and the weights, in pounds, of four randomly selected men. The corresponding linear regression line fitted using this sample is $\overset{^}{\,y}=-165+4.6x.$
Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, $\overset{―}{x}=70,$ and $\text{MSE}=3.6,$ find a $90%$ confidence interval for the $y$-intercept of the regression line.

*Hint: Use the fact that $P(T>2.920)=0.05,$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $2$ degrees of freedom. Also, the standard error for the $y$-intecept is* 

$$
\text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}\,]=\sqrt{\text{MSE}\cdot (\frac{1}{n}+\frac{{\overset{―}{x}}^{2}}{{S}_{xx}})}.
$$
worked_solution:
We use the following notations:

- $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ is the regression line that best fits the population, and

- $\overset{^}{\,y}={\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}+{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}x$ is the estimate of the "true" regression line given by the data in our sample.

In this case, we have that  

$$
\overset{^}{\,y}={\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}+{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}x=-165+4.6x.
$$

We are told that all assumptions for a simple regression model are held. So, given a value $\alpha $ between $0$ and $1,$ the corresponding $[100(1-\alpha )]%$ confidence interval for the $y$-intercept ${\beta }_{0}$ of our model can be written as

$$
{\beta }_{0}\,\pm \,\overset{\text{margin of error}}{\overset{⏞}{{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}\cdot \text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}\,]}}.
$$

Note the following:

- $\,{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}$ is our point estimate for the intercept, computed using the data points from our sample.

- $P(T>{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2})=\frac{\alpha }{2},$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $n-2$ degrees of freedom.

- $\text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}\,]$ is the standard error of ${\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0},$ given by

$$
\text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}\,]=\sqrt{\text{MSE}\cdot (\frac{1}{n}+\frac{{\overset{―}{x}}^{2}}{{S}_{xx}})}
$$

where we have:

- $\text{MSE}$ is the mean squared error of the model:

$$
\text{MSE}=\frac{1}{n-2}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-{\overset{^}{\,y}}_{i})^{2}
$$

where ${\overset{^}{\,y}}_{i}$ is the estimate of ${y}_{i}$ given by our regression model.

- ${S}_{xx}$ is the usual sum of squares formula:

$$
{S}_{xx}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}
$$

- **Step 1.** Find the point estimate. From the regression equation $\overset{^}{\,y}=-165+4.6x,$ our point estimate is

$$
{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}=-165.
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the margin of error. 

- Since we are interested in finding a $90%$ confidence interval, we have 

$$
\alpha =1-0.9=0.1\,⟹\,\frac{\alpha }{2}=0.05.
$$

We are given that $P(T>2.920)=0.05.$ As a result, 

$$
{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}={t}_{2,0.05}=2.920.
$$

- Computing ${S}_{xx},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} & =(64-70)^{2}+(68-70)^{2}+(72-70)^{2}+(76-70)^{2} \\  & =36+4+4+36 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

- Now, we can compute the margin of error:

$$
{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}\cdot \text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}\,]=2.920\cdot \sqrt{3.6\cdot (\frac{1}{4}+\frac{{70}^{2}}{80})}≈43.4
$$

- **Step 3.** Determine the limits of the confidence interval:

$$
{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}\,\pm \,{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}\cdot \text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}\,]=-165\pm 43.4
$$

β0±tn−2,α/2⋅SE[β^0]⏞margin of error.

    β^0=−165.
